semantic_spot_checks.claim: The study enrolled and analyzed 74 HFS patients (56 female, 18 male).
Overall SF-36 rose from 57.4 ± 2.4 at baseline to 61.3 ± 3.0 at 27 months and declined to 52.1 ± 4.2 at 54 months (p=0.002).
The general-health subdomain improved across five years (p=0.02), while several other annualized SF-36 domains worsened at years 4-5.
CES-D did not significantly improve in sequential analysis (p=0.924).
Abo-BTX A was administered as 100 units IM every three months, 25 units at each of four facial sites.

extraction_limitations: The source does not report visit-specific denominators/attrition in the Results text.
The article does not provide dedicated adverse-event incidence data or neutralizing-antibody testing.
The Results narrative contains a likely labeling inconsistency at the 45-month 15.9 ± 2.3 value; the atom preserves and tags this source inconsistency rather than silently correcting it.

source.title: The Five-Year Prospective Study of Quality of Life in Hemifacial Spasm Treated with Abo-Botulinum Toxin A

semantic_spot_checks.claim: Only the SF-36 general-health domain showed persistent/significant improvement across five years (p=0.02), while several other QoL measures worsened late.
Overall SF-36 was 57.4 ± 2.4 at baseline, 61.3 ± 3.0 at 27 months, and 52.1 ± 4.2 at 54 months (p=0.002).
The study is single-arm, participants had substantial prior Abo-BTX exposure, visit-specific denominators are not reported, and neutralizing antibodies were not tested.
semantic_spot_checks.note: The first three items are design/reporting appraisal derived directly from source structure/content; antibody non-testing is explicitly discussed by authors.

semantic_spot_checks.claim: Figure 4 reports annualized general-health improvement (p=0.02) and worsening at years 4-5 in physical-health, physical-functioning, and emotional subdomains (p=0.04, 0.03, 0.03).
Figure 5 and Methods specify 25 U Abo-BTX A at four ipsilateral orbicularis sites for 100 U total per session.

warnings: Source Figure 4 caption contains ambiguous/duplicated panel labels; SEA explicitly notes this.
The source Results text has a likely HFS-30/AIMS labeling inconsistency around a 45-month 15.9 ± 2.3 value; SEA does not use this ambiguity to overstate a conclusion.
